transcript.text:
Sorry to hear that! Here are some common causes and fixes, grouped by symptom.

## First, quick checks (solve a surprising number of problems)
• Power: Is it plugged in and switched on at the wall? Try another appliance in the same socket, and check your fuse box for a tripped switch.
• Door: Close it firmly. Most dryers won't start if the door switch doesn't register.
• Child lock: Many models have one. Check your manual for how to turn it off, which is often done by holding a button for a few seconds.
• Delay timer: Make sure a delayed start hasn't been set by accident.
• Reset: Unplug it for 5–10 minutes, then try again.

## By symptom

It won't turn on at all
• Check the plug fuse (UK plugs usually have a 13A fuse you can swap).
• A faulty door switch or blown thermal fuse is common. These are cheap parts but need some DIY confidence.

It turns on but the drum doesn't spin
• Most likely a broken drive belt. If the drum turns very easily by hand, the belt has probably snapped.
• Overloading can also stop it, so try a smaller load.

The drum spins but there's no heat
• Clean the lint filter. A clogged filter can trigger overheating protection.
• Condenser dryers: Empty the water tank and rinse the condenser unit.
• Vented dryers: Check the hose for kinks, crushing, or lint blockages.
• If those are fine, it may be a heating element, thermostat, or thermal fuse fault.

It works but takes ages to dry
• Clean the lint filter (ideally after every load).
• Clean the condenser or check the vent hose.
• Don't overload it, and make sure clothes have been spun well in the washer first.
• Make sure the room isn't very cold or damp, especially for heat pump dryers.

It shows an error code
• Note the code and look it up in your manual or on the manufacturer's website. It usually points straight to the problem.

## Safety
• Always unplug the dryer before opening it up or doing anything beyond basic cleaning.
• If you smell burning, stop using it immediately.
• If it's a gas dryer, leave internal repairs to a Gas Safe registered engineer.

---

To narrow it down, could you tell me:
1. What exactly is happening? For example, no power, no heat, drum not turning, or an error code.
2. The make and model.
3. The type: vented, condenser, or heat pump.

With those details I can give you more specific steps.
It's a Hotpoint condenser. Lights come on but when I press start nothing happens, no sound at all. Started this morning, door had felt loose for a few days.

A door that felt loose for a few days, followed by a dryer that powers up but won't start, almost always points to the door catch or door switch. The dryer needs to sense the door is fully shut before it will start. If the latch isn't holding the door tight against the switch, it stays silent exactly as you describe.

## Quick test
1. Close the door firmly.
2. Press and hold the door shut with one hand, near the handle side.
3. Press Start with the other.

If it starts: That confirms the door catch or switch. Let it stop and don't keep holding it shut as a workaround.
If it still does nothing: Skip to "Other things to rule out" below.

## What to check (unplug first)
• The catch on the door: It's the small plastic hook or tongue on the door edge. Look for cracks, wear, or a broken piece. These snap or wear down quite often on Hotpoints.
• The hinge: Open the door and check whether it sags or wobbles. Loose hinge screws can misalign the catch so it no longer engages the switch. Tightening them sometimes fixes it completely.
• The slot in the frame: Make sure it's not blocked with lint or debris and nothing looks broken inside.

## Fixing it
• Parts: A Hotpoint door catch or door switch is usually inexpensive (often around £10–30). Find your model number on a sticker inside the door rim, then search "[model number] door switch" or "door catch."
• Door catch: It's usually a simple swap, held on by a couple of screws or clips.
• Door switch: It sits behind the front panel, so it's a bit more involved but manageable with basic DIY skills and a YouTube guide for your model.
• Don't tape, wedge, or bypass the switch. It stops the drum running with the door open.

## Other things to rule out
• Empty water tank light: If it's on, empty the tank and reseat it fully.
• Child lock: Look for a key or padlock symbol. On many Hotpoints you hold a button (or two) for about 3 seconds to unlock.
• Delay timer: Check one isn't set.
• Reset: Unplug it for 10 minutes, then try again.

## Safety recall check
Hotpoint condenser dryers made roughly 2004–2015 were part of a fire safety recall. Enter your model and serial number on the Whirlpool UK safety recall website to check. If yours is affected, the fix is free.

If the hold-the-door test doesn't start it, let me know your model number and any lights showing, and I can help narrow it down further.
Tried holding the door shut and pressing start, it runs while I hold it and stops when I let go. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the bit on the floor.

That confirms it: the snapped tongue on the door catch is the whole problem. The dryer is working fine otherwise. This is one of the cheapest and easiest dryer repairs.

## 1. Find your model number
Open the door and look for a sticker around the door rim or frame. It'll be something like "TCFS 83B" or "NV4D 01P." Write it down or photograph it.

## 2. Order the part
• Search "[your model number] door catch" or "door latch."
• Try Hotpoint's own spares site, or parts retailers like eSpares, Partmaster, or Amazon. Expect roughly £5–20.
• Keep the broken piece so you can compare it with the photos before ordering. Catches vary between models.

## 3. Fit it (unplug first)
The exact method depends on your model, but it's usually one of these:
• Clip-in catch: Some just push or twist into place on the door edge.
• Screw-held catch: More commonly, you open the door and remove the screws around the inner door panel to separate it from the outer panel. The catch sits between the two. Swap it, then screw the panels back together.

Search YouTube for "Hotpoint [model number] door catch replacement" for a step-by-step guide. It's typically 10–20 minutes with a screwdriver.

While the door's open, tighten the hinge screws too. A sagging door may be what stressed the catch.

## In the meantime
• Don't run it by holding or wedging the door shut.
• Gluing the tongue back on usually fails quickly because of the pressure the latch takes each time you close it. A new part is cheap and much more reliable.

## Worth a 1-minute check
Hotpoint, which is owned by Whirlpool, ran a safety modification programme and recall on many condenser and vented dryers made between 2004 and 2015. If yours might be from that era, enter your model and serial number on Whirlpool's UK dryer safety checker to make sure it's not affected.
